quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders to carry a passenger safely. The motorcycle should also have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear protective gear just like you do.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle operator should be ready for:

options.text: Open parking spaces.
A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
Parking meters.
Other drivers to see you and move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for one to suddenly pull out into traffic. It is safest to ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and any dangers.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle operator?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots that support your ankles give the best protection. High-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If your boots have long laces, tuck them away securely before riding.

questions.question: Proper motorcycle riding clothing should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Cover your arms but leave your legs exposed.
Cover your legs but leave your arms exposed.
Be whatever is most comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: For safe riding, wear a jacket and pants that completely cover your arms and legs.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These regulatory signs tell you the rules of the road, and you must follow them.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Ignore them.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass you. Speeding up makes them tailgate you at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: Your normal scanning routine should include:

options.text: Frequent head checks.
Frequent body checks.
Turning your entire body to look at your surroundings.
Keeping your eyes focused only in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequent head checks.
questions.explanation: Make frequent head checks part of your normal scanning routine. Knowing what is happening all around you helps you prepare for any situation.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicle lights.
Harder than riding during the day because visibility is poor.
Not allowed on highways.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because visibility is poor.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because it is harder to see and be seen. Without normal shadows and light, it is harder to judge distances.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass your vehicle when possible. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, increasing danger.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?

options.text: By the left handgrip
By the right handgrip
By the left footrest
By the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located near the left handgrip. Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride.

questions.question: What is it called when you shift to a lower gear?

options.text: Engine braking.
Acceleration.
Upshifting.
Coasting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear creates an effect similar to braking. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: Eyeballing the tire is a good method.
Use a tire gauge.
It is best to squeeze the tire.
Compare the height of the tire to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure before every ride. A tire can look okay even if it is under-inflated, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Maintain a space cushion between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to monitor traffic behind you.
Look for opportunities to squeeze through the stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a space cushion between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or another vehicle approaches from behind.

questions.question: What should you do when riding a motorcycle you are not familiar with?

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition.
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride as you usually do, since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: All motorcycles are different. Before riding, get familiar with the bike. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn the gear pattern.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is allowed?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and complete the pass within a passing zone.
You should sound your horn to get the other driver to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and complete the pass within a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen only in areas where passing is safe and legal. You must start and finish the pass within a passing zone.

questions.question: What can you do in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass another vehicle if the pass can be completed before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chances of being in a crash?

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep your intentions unknown from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake light, and correct lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when riding?

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Are not as effective at protecting your eyes as eyeglasses.
Are not effective in providing any protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. Only a face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When you must ride over an obstacle or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Speed up.
Swerve quickly.
Rise slightly off the seat to allow your legs to absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat to allow your legs to absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise off your seat so your legs can absorb the impact. Just before impact, roll on the throttle slightly to lighten the front end.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: Change lanes.
Direct another driver's attention away from your vehicle.
Show other drivers that an exit is approaching.
Invite other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Turn off your signal after your maneuver is complete.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use the emergency brake only.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. This applies to all stops, not just emergencies.

questions.question: If you have been drinking alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide if you can ride based on how you feel.
Set a drinking limit so you can still ride safely.
Not ride.
Ride if you feel fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride.
questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet has all of the following except:

options.text: An impact-resistant outer shell.
An impact-absorbing inner liner.
A chinstrap retention system.
Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: When checking your motorcycle before riding, make sure that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Check each brake lever before every ride. Press each one to make sure it feels firm and holds the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Because most crashes happen during the day, it is important to:

options.text: Not ride during the day.
Wear brightly-colored clothing when riding.
Wear sunglasses when riding.
Ride on the shoulder as much as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing when riding.
questions.explanation: Wear brightly-colored clothing every time you ride. This helps other drivers see you, even during the day.
